DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.636.standard: BNF minimum standards, NICE CG178 and SIGN 131: side-effect review after initiation and dose titration, at 3 months and annually (gold standard adds 1 month); GASS form completion

cycle1.result: GASS completion rate 7% across both wards; only 1 form valid; one ward had no completed forms

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.636.intervention: Presentation at ward QI meetings, infographic for staff, highlighting role and importance of the forms; re-audit after 2 months

cycle2.result: Completion rate rose from 7% to 26% (3 to 9 patients); valid forms increased from 1 to 4

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.636.other_findings: Improvement described as sub-optimal; patient acuity limited completion.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.273.setting: Nottingham City Central Local Mental Health Team (community)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.273.standard: MHRA guidance that clozapine levels should be monitored in clinical situations where toxicity may be suspected

cycle1.dates: Plasma levels 2006 to 2020; doses from 2018 onwards
cycle1.result: 273 clozapine levels taken; mean interval between levels 10 months 2 weeks (range 2 days to 13 years); 88 levels >600 ug/L and 108 levels <350 ug/L; 32% of levels above recommended range; non-significant positive dose-level trend (R = 0.37)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.273.other_findings: No routine clozapine level monitoring found; unclear whether levels were trough levels.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.556.topic: Antidepressant indication documentation and medication review
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.556.setting: Hailsham Early Intervention in Psychosis Service
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.556.standard: Diagnosis recorded alongside each antidepressant prescription; EIPN guidance that psychotropic medication is reviewed every 6 months

cycle1.result: 33 patients (37%) prescribed an antidepressant; 25 (76%) had a recorded indication; 67 patients (84%) had a medical review within 6 months

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.556.other_findings: Sertraline was the commonest antidepressant (52%); re-audit planned in 6 months.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.095.topic: Raised inflammatory markers of unclear cause
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.095.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath, rheumatology outpatients

cycle1.result: Mean referral to seen time 3.43 weeks; 36% mechanical or non-rheumatological diagnosis, 34% inflammatory arthritis; diagnosis changed in 25% on follow-up; 6 deaths (13% mortality)

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.095.other_findings: Autoimmune testing in 97% and radiology in 90%; 3 new malignancies diagnosed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.302.topic: Vitamin D testing and replacement in inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.302.setting: Becklin Centre, acute adult psychiatric inpatient unit, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.302.standard: Trust policy that vitamin D is checked in all inpatients and supplementation started where appropriate; target 90% for both

cycle1.result: Vitamin D checked in 79 (56.4%); colecalciferol started in 61 (83.6%) of those insufficient or deficient; target not met

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.302.intervention: Planned presentation of findings to the Trust medical workforce
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.302.other_findings: Testing rate differed by ethnicity (Caucasian 64.0% vs non-Caucasian 44.4%, p = 0.032); 51.9% insufficient and 40.5% deficient.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.271.setting: Tertiary hepato-pancreato-biliary unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.271.standard: PACT-UK synoptic reporting template for pancreatic cancer CT; compliance defined as more than 90% of information available

cycle1.result: Compliance 0% for initial presentation scans and 4.2% (n=1) of 24 staging scans; the only compliant scan used the PACT-UK template

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.271.other_findings: More than 80% of reports lacked pancreatic duct size, predicted tumour type and stage, variant vascular anatomy and arterial/venous involvement.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.484.topic: Psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.484.setting: Crisis Team, Fieldhead Hospital, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.484.standard: NICE guidelines on psychotropic prescribing, baseline investigations, review and physical health monitoring

cycle1.result: 100% for indication, dosage, discussion with patient and side-effect monitoring; of 22 on antipsychotics, 11 had ECG and bloods by Crisis Team, 4 by other parties, 3 bloods but no ECG, 2 no physical health monitoring

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.484.other_findings: 46 of 50 responded to treatment; physical health monitoring needs improvement.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11706.setting: Kilbarrack East Community Mental Health Team, North Dublin Mental Health Services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11706.standard: NICE guidelines for lithium monitoring (lithium levels, renal and thyroid function, calcium, BMI)

cycle1.result: 12% (3/25) compliant with all lithium monitoring guidelines; none had calcium or BMI recorded

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11706.intervention: MDT meeting; green sticker system, lithium monitoring sheet, patient monitoring lists defining responsibilities, lithium blood clinic and new Clinical Nurse Specialist reporting system (March 2025)

cycle2.result: 68% (17/25) compliant; 32% (8/25) had no lithium level; 44% had no U&E or thyroid tests; 8% had calcium tested; no BMI recorded

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11706.other_findings: Patient education leaflet introduced after the second audit; calcium and BMI stayed poor.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001088.topic: Antibiotic prescribing audit and feedback in nursing homes
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001088.setting: Nursing home physicians receiving MyPractice: Long-Term Care reports, Ontario

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001088.other_findings: Qualitative interview study; professional role and identity influenced antibiotic prescribing and response to the feedback report.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.538.standard: NICE guidance on ECT: documented risk/benefit assessment including anaesthetic risk and cognitive impairment, patient information leaflet, consultation of advocate

cycle1.result: Indication documented 100%; RCPsych leaflet received 50%; risk/benefit discussion documented 50%; specific side effects discussed 50%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.538.other_findings: Standardised consent form being considered, with re-audit planned after introduction.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.258.topic: BMI recording and dietetic referral on admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.258.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards and PICU, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.258.standard: BMI measured and recorded after admission; referral to dietetics if BMI >30 kg/m2, or >28 kg/m2 with weight-related comorbidities

cycle1.result: No BMI measured on admission for 14 of 148; 34 met referral criteria, of whom 4 were not referred and 5 declined

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.258.other_findings: 74 of 134 with BMI recorded were overweight or obese; need to emphasise BMI recording in the admission physical health screen.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10609.setting: General adult psychiatry wards 19 and 20, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10609.standard: Scottish Patient Safety Programme and NICE: 95% of medicines reconciled within 24 hours of admission; local medicines reconciliation guidelines

cycle1.result: 70% of forms completed within 24 hours; two sources of information used in 66%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10609.intervention: Summary document of latest guidelines and link to an e-learning module distributed to resident doctors and raised at monthly resident doctors' meeting

cycle2.result: 100% of forms completed within 24 hours; two sources used in 100%; improvement in all 12 areas assessed

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10609.other_findings: Results may reflect individual variability between clerking doctors.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11712.setting: North and South Community Mental Health Teams, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11712.standard: Trust standard (NHS Standard Contract): 100% of clinic outcomes completed within 24 hours and clinic letters within 7 days

cycle1.result: Clinic entries within 24 hours: South 99%, North 94%; letters within 7 days: South 99%, North 92%; 8% of North letters overdue or missing, some up to 31 days

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11712.other_findings: Recommended presenting findings, an administrative capacity survey and a 12-week re-audit.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.252.setting: Rheumatology department, St George's NHS Foundation Trust, London (tertiary)

cycle1.result: 59 (60%) taking corticosteroids at scan; 39.8% showed active rheumatological disease; 32.6% non-rheumatological abnormalities; 2% new cancer diagnoses

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.252.other_findings: Incidental findings led to further tests including ultrasound (11 patients) and endoscopy (7 patients).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.217.topic: Dual diagnosis substance misuse assessment on admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.217.setting: Redbridge Community Recovery Team West, psychiatric admissions
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.217.standard: NICE CG120 on co-existing severe mental illness and substance misuse (used to guide recommendations)

cycle1.result: Only 50% with known dual diagnosis had a urine drug screen on admission; 25% of those currently misusing substances were referred to specialist services

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.217.other_findings: Dual diagnosis patients were more often detained (89% vs 72%), of no fixed abode (28% vs 13%) and non-compliant pre-admission (83% vs 56%).

DOI:10.1111/anae.16413.topic: Peri-operative cardiac arrest in cardiology procedures
DOI:10.1111/anae.16413.setting: 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: 54/881 (6.1%) of NAP7 cardiac arrest reports; estimated incidence 1/450 or 0.22 (0.17–0.29)%; ECMO CPR 3/53 (6%)

DOI:10.1111/anae.16413.other_findings: Themes included logistics and teamworking in remote locations, cardiogenic shock, late anaesthetic involvement and TAVI.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.429.topic: Risk assessment on admission to mixed-sex wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.429.setting: Mixed-sex inpatient psychiatric wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.429.standard: Acute care group standard: patients with known risk to the opposite sex not admitted to mixed-sex wards; comprehensive risk assessment on admission with escalation to MDT

cycle1.result: Full risk assessment documented in 50%; historical risks in 40%; clerkings contained a risk assessment in 70%; 30% had risks to the opposite sex, none escalated to MDT

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.429.other_findings: Recommended specific guidance and teaching; re-audit scheduled for March 2022.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11564.setting: Beech Unit, Torbay, Devon Partnership Trust (inpatient)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11564.standard: Trust Inpatient Admissions SOP: capacity to consent to treatment assessed within 24 hours of admission; MCA Code of Practice (decision-specific, four-part functional test, least restrictive, best interests)

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment within 24 hours 100%; MCA template completed in 90% (half within timeframe); decision documented 90%; functional test 90%; least restrictive and best interests 53%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11564.other_findings: Recommended using the Trust standardised MCA template and guidance for clerking doctors.

PMID:29570544.setting: 35 acute care hospitals in 7 countries (International Collaboration of Orthopaedic Nursing)
PMID:29570544.standard: 12 internationally accepted nursing quality care indicators for older adults with fragility hip fracture

cycle1.result: 35 hospitals (100%) completed the audit; quality indicators were reflected in the majority of policies, protocols or processes, with variable timing and frequency

PMID:29570544.other_findings: Development and testing of an audit tool; respondents found content relevant and applicable.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.398.setting: Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.398.standard: NICE NG108 (2018) recommendations 1.4: 100% of admitted patients should have MCA completed during admission clerking

cycle1.result: MCA completed with capacity at clerking and review in 85%; lacked capacity at clerking 3%; capacity at admission but not at review 5%; MCA not completed or unavailable in 7%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.398.other_findings: Discrepancy between clerking and later reviews suggests further training needed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.430.setting: Medium secure forensic hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.430.standard: NICE: all patients with psychosis offered CBTp and complete at least 16 sessions

cycle1.result: 68% (19/28) offered CBTp; 85% (11/13) of these completed 16 sessions

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.430.other_findings: Barriers to offering were being too unwell (7/9) or in other therapies (2/9); barrier to completion was patient refusal (2/2).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10647.topic: Primary care mental health practitioner assessment and referral
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10647.setting: Community Mental Health Team, Brentwood Resource Centre
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10647.standard: All new referrals first seen by the Mental Health Practitioner; MHP PCN Consultation V2 assessment template used; target 100%

cycle1.result: Referrals initially assessed 69.2% (82.5%); GP referrals compliant 67.2% (80.2%); MHP assessment template used 100%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10647.other_findings: 190 (24.5%) did not engage and 44 (5.7%) had data unavailable.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.497.setting: Community secondary mental health service, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 44% (n = 40) smokers; 31 offered smoking cessation advice; NRT offered to 13; 5 referred to smoking cessation services

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.497.other_findings: Survey: 20/31 smokers wanted to reduce or quit; local GPs did not prescribe NRT and no targeted community service existed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10424.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics in dementia: initiation for severe agitation/distress under specialist supervision, monitoring and follow-up

cycle1.result: 24 of 63 with dementia on antipsychotics; blood monitoring 56% (13/24); ECG 50% (12/24); follow-up plan 81% (51/63); reduction plan 8% (2/24)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10424.other_findings: 8% (5/95) on antipsychotics without dementia diagnosis; an antipsychotic register was suggested.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.627.topic: Mental Health Act detention by ethnicity
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.627.setting: Andersen Ward Mother and Baby Unit, South Manchester

cycle1.result: Detained: Black 88%, Asian 72.7%, Mixed/other 33.3%, White 28.3% (statistically significant); all 11 with non-English primary language detained

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.627.other_findings: Length of stay and time to first section 17 leave did not differ by ethnicity.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.099.topic: Mortality risk documentation in emergency laparotomy consent
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.099.setting: West Suffolk Hospital, Bury St Edmunds, emergency general surgery
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.099.standard: NCEPOD 2011: risk of mortality explicitly discussed and documented on consent forms and in medical records

cycle1.result: Mortality documented in NELA 93%, consent forms 40%, medical notes discussion 35%

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.099.intervention: Periodic reminders for surgeons during meetings and posters

cycle2.result: Mortality documented in NELA 90%, consent forms 92%, medical notes 51% (consent improvement p < 0.0001)

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.099.other_findings: Three cycles; second cycle (March to May 2022, 38 cases) showed 92% NELA, 71% consent forms and 42% notes.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.96.topic: Eating disorder referral quality in CAMHS
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.96.setting: West Glasgow CAMHS team, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.96.standard: Junior MARSIPAN guidelines for referral content and physical measures

cycle1.result: Height and weight recorded in 73.1% of referrals

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.96.intervention: Duty clinicians screened referrals and prompted GPs for physical parameters; weekly board round meeting; weekly physical health monitoring clinic

cycle2.result: Height and weight recorded in 82.1%; 53.8% needed prompting; risk recorded 46.2%, onset 51.3%, body image 56.4% (no change in written content); mean referral to diagnosis 44.1 to 34.2 days

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.96.other_findings: Staff stress (MHPSS) scores stayed high; a GP referral proforma was recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.261.setting: Older adult inpatient units across four localities, Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.261.standard: NICE CG183: 100% of drug charts and electronic records (Rio) have allergy status documented

cycle1.result: Paper drug charts 100% (type or severity 70%); EPR allergy status 62% (range 30–100% by ward; Wolverhampton 93%, West Bromwich 100%, Dudley 33%, Walsall 39%)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.261.intervention: Allergy status prompt in electronic clerking document, stickers and posters, pharmacy updating EPR allergy status, allergy alert on bed state view
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.261.other_findings: Second data collection of around 300 patients was under way.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.48.standard: Local vancomycin prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring guidance

cycle1.result: Loading, initial continuous dosing and TDM generally in line with local guidelines; 9% of first levels subtherapeutic; of 298 levels 56% therapeutic, 19% supratherapeutic, 25% subtherapeutic

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.48.other_findings: A previous audit of intermittent dosing found 50% of first levels subtherapeutic; no vancomycin-specific adverse effects.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.470.topic: Driving risk assessment and DVLA advice
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.470.setting: Adult acute inpatient wards, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.470.standard: Local policy: leave risk discussion capturing driving risk before home leave; DVLA advice documented in notes and discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Leave risk discussion compliance 73%; 5% of drivers given written DVLA guidance on discharge letters

cycle2.result: 100% compliance with leave risk discussion; 56% had DVLA advice recorded on discharge summary

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.470.other_findings: Improvement plan agreed: MDT communication, junior doctor induction and driving advice added to discharge meeting checklist.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.428.topic: Community and inpatient team interface during admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.428.setting: Elm Ward (female inpatients), West Park Hospital, Darlington
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.428.standard: Trust Admission, Transfer and Discharge policy (community team involvement, care plan copy, GP informed within 24 hours of admission)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.dates: Discharges 1 February 2021 to 23 March 2021; data collected May 2021
cycle2.result: Community team invited to meetings in 96%; contact with community team in 100%; GP informed increased to 20%; written care plan copy offered increased but still low; overall amber rating

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.428.other_findings: Expected length of stay was poorly communicated by care coordinators and responsibility for informing GPs was unclear.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.055.topic: Acute upper GI bleeding care bundle
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.055.setting: Single surgical unit, University Hospital Hairmyres, East Kilbride
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.055.standard: BSG-led multisociety AUGIB care bundle (2019); target 100% for each step

cycle1.result: All OGDs had consultant supervision; significant gap in applying the care bundle, Glasgow-Blatchford risk scoring and resuscitation and medical management (detailed figures in table, not given in text)

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.055.other_findings: 30-day mortality 8.0%; 56.7% of OGDs in hours; recommended formal implementation of the bundle from ED to admission unit.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.437.setting: Victoria Ward, old age psychiatry, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.437.standard: BMA, BNF and Trust prescription writing standards (GMC number, signature, doctor's name, drug, indication, dose, route, frequency, start date, date, timings)

cycle1.result: Errors found in all parameters except medication timings

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.437.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and re-training on prescription writing

cycle2.result: Errors increased: GMC number errors up 20.33%, doctor's name 16.87%, indication 12.94%, original start date 5%; name of drug improved by 10.88%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.437.other_findings: Trust then issued stamps with GMC number and doctor's name to junior doctors; re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.630.setting: Adult PICU, Park House Hospital, Greater Manchester Mental Health
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.630.standard: Local trust seclusion policy (physical health, risk, medication, MSE review; initial medical review within 60 minutes)

cycle1.result: Initiation time and rationale 95%; physical health 75%; risk to others 50%; risk to self 5%; MSE and medication review 50%; initial medical review within 60 minutes 44%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.630.other_findings: Policy since changed to 'overall psychiatric health'; risk to self largely undocumented.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.105.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.105.setting: Older persons mental health inpatient units, three sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.105.standard: NICE and Department of Health VTE guidelines; target 100%

cycle1.result: East: 6/9 forms filled; Central: 2 of 21 had a form, none filled; West: 3 of 11 had a completed form; no standard proforma in Central or West

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.105.intervention: Trust-wide VTE risk assessment proforma adapted for psychiatric inpatients planned
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.105.other_findings: VTE prophylaxis mentioned inconsistently on medication charts.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.604.setting: Lithium clinic, Older Person's Mental Health Service, Princess of Wales Hospital (district general hospital)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.604.standard: NICE lithium guidance and GMC Good Medical Practice; 100% of relevant data documented

cycle1.result: Dose, level and renal function over 83.3% (n = 15); psychotropics 61.1%; side effects 50%; mood 77.8%; safety netting 11.1% (n = 2)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.604.intervention: Results disseminated to team and lithium clinic proforma introduced, revised after clinician feedback

cycle2.result: Dose, levels, psychotropics and side effects 100% (n = 12); renal function and mood 91.7% (n = 11); safety netting 75% (n = 9)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.604.other_findings: Documentation varied between clinicians before the proforma.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10619.setting: Psychiatry units, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10619.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry, 13th edition, pre-clozapine assessment

cycle1.result: FBC, LFT, U&E and glucose 100%; ECG 76%; lipids 33%; ESR 19%; troponin 14%; CRP, BNP and physical examination 0%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10619.other_findings: Barriers included staff training, prescriber inconsistency and funding and staffing limits.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.577.standard: National guidance on pre-lithium checks (weight/BMI/waist, TFTs, calcium, eGFR), POMH lithium audit

cycle1.result: Weight/BMI/waist 78%; calcium 80%; TFTs 93%; eGFR 100% before initiation; all above national POMH compliance

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.577.intervention: Planned Quality Performance Alert to medical and nursing staff and lithium monitoring in junior doctor induction

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.257.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.257.standard: Trust recommendations for high-dose antipsychotic therapy (clozapine considered; baseline and post-increase ECG, BMI, BP, pulse, bloods)

cycle1.result: 21 on combination therapy, 11 on HDAT; clozapine considered in 9 of 11 HDAT; ECG before HDAT 100% but after dose increase 36%; BMI 100%; BP and pulse 91%; HbA1c 91%; prolactin 46%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.257.other_findings: HDAT prevalence 9% against 28% in the 2012 POMH audit.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.360.topic: Weight and BMI monitoring in learning disability
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.360.setting: Tower Hamlets Community Learning Disability Service, East London Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.360.standard: Project target: up-to-date BMI for 70% or more of service users by September 2024

cycle1.result: 26.7% of 71 service users had an updated weight and BMI

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.360.intervention: Planned PDSA cycles; weekly MDT meetings with service users; waiting-room machine for weight, height and blood pressure; staff education
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.360.other_findings: No robust process for weight monitoring across a caseload of 1264.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.486.setting: 17-bed functional old age psychiatry ward, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.486.standard: Electronic admission clerking pro forma based on Royal College of Psychiatrists admission guidelines; 90% compliance with each section

cycle1.result: All domains improved from 2019 to 2021 except mental state examination (9.09% decrease, not significant); 4 domains improved significantly; 9 domains still below the 90% standard

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.486.other_findings: Comparison of pre-pandemic and pandemic periods rather than a pre/post intervention audit; late pandemic better in 10 domains, early pandemic better in 4.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10700.topic: Relapse prevention medication in detox referrals
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10700.setting: The Level Nottingham inpatient detoxification unit (referrals from community addiction services)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10700.standard: Referrals mention relapse prevention medications and provide blood test results; target 100% for each

cycle1.result: RPMs not mentioned in 40% of alcohol and 77% of opioid referrals; 48% of referrals had no blood results; median 22 days from blood results to referral and 85 days to admission

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10700.other_findings: About one-third of referrals did not mention RPMs and were not going to residential rehabilitation; recommended referrer discussions and referral form changes.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.624.topic: Controlled drug prescription writing in opioid substitution therapy
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.624.setting: Substance misuse service issuing methadone and buprenorphine prescriptions
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.624.standard: Legal requirements for controlled drug prescriptions and Home Office approved instalment wording; internal script record standard terms

cycle1.result: 100% met legal CD requirements; 7 (11%) omitted Home Office wording for pharmacy closure days; 46 (72%) had non-applicable additional wording; 13 different frequency terms used in script record against 6 standard terms

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.624.other_findings: Frequency of collection left blank on 2 occasions.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.055.setting: Rheumatology service, Pennine MSK Partnership, Oldham
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.055.standard: ACR and EULAR guidance supporting biologic tapering; locally agreed eligibility criteria

cycle1.result: Patients tapered increased from 24 in 2019 to 51 in 2021; tapering failed in 7/116 (6%); estimated saving up to £170,000 per annum

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.055.intervention: EHR records flagged to prompt shared decision-making discussion at routine appointments
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.055.other_findings: More patients were eligible than identified by EHR search because of missing coding (787, 61%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.260.topic: Physical health monitoring on psychiatric admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.260.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.260.standard: Trust policy: physical health monitoring within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours: BMI 91%, blood pressure 62%, cholesterol 59%, HbA1c 58%; QRISK calculated in 78% of eligible; NRT offered to 97% of smokers (13% accepted)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.260.other_findings: A 24-hour physical health checklist was suggested.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11705.standard: BNF annual monitoring of weight, glucose/HbA1c, lipids and blood pressure: 100% with three or more of four monitored; 80% monitored for each measure

cycle1.result: 48% had three or more risk factors monitored; overall monitoring rate 58%; no measure reached 80%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11705.intervention: Recommendations from the first cycle (details not reported)

cycle2.result: 60% had three or more risk factors monitored; overall monitoring rate 65% (p = 0.04); no measure reached 80%, three measures improved

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11705.other_findings: Further recommendations: manual reminders for patients outside SMI checks and phlebotomy access; re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11573.topic: Leave and observation documentation in admission plans
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11573.standard: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and local risk protocols: MHA status, leave and observation levels documented

cycle1.result: Observation levels documented 15.4%; leave status documented 1.9% (13.5% failed to mention leave at all); MHA status 82.7%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11573.intervention: Posters in resident doctor work areas prompting legal status and safety monitoring plans

cycle2.result: Observation levels 55.2%; leave status 65.5%; MHA status 75.9%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11573.other_findings: MHA status documentation stayed roughly the same.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa109.setting: Rheumatology, Royal Surrey County Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Guildford
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa109.standard: NICE and BSR: DAS28 recorded at least every 6 months for patients with RA on high-cost DMARDs

cycle1.result: 166 (80%) had a documented DAS28; 14 (7%) had DAS28 at least 6-monthly; 152 (73%) did not meet the standard

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa109.other_findings: Scores were recorded on Blueteq but not in letters; a DAS28 table in the clinic letter template was suggested.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.238.topic: Bone protection in giant cell arteritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.238.setting: Rheumatology, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.238.standard: BSR giant cell arteritis guideline: consider pharmacological bone protection at presentation

cycle1.result: Bisphosphonate consideration documented at diagnosis in 96% overall (TOC 94%, MTX 91%, MONO 100%); compliance for recommended duration 88% overall

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.238.other_findings: No significant difference between steroid-sparing and monotherapy groups (p = 0.52 and 0.8).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11846.setting: Inpatient psychiatric unit, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11846.standard: NICE guidelines and local Trust policy on insomnia (non-pharmacological first, CBT-I, documented indication, review and stop dates for hypnotics)

cycle1.result: Insomnia in 30 (66.6%); documented in 23 (76.6%); sleep hygiene in 11/30 (36.6%); CBT-I offered 0%; hypnotics offered to 26/30 (86.6%); 0% met all NICE and Trust criteria

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11846.other_findings: A standardised insomnia care pathway was recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10689.setting: Southern Gambling Service (outpatient gambling disorder service)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10689.standard: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care and Royal College of Physicians guidance: full AUDIT if AUDIT-C at least 5, brief intervention for scores 5–10, advice and signposting for 11 or more

cycle1.result: AUDIT-C and EWAC completed 100%; full AUDIT 0%; brief intervention documented in 7% of higher-risk; 1 (25%) possibly dependent patient signposted; none given advice on avoiding abrupt cessation

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10689.intervention: Recommended: full AUDIT for AUDIT-C 5 or more, staff upskilling in brief intervention, regional alcohol services directory, psychoeducation materials
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10689.other_findings: 98 patients referred; all with scores of 11 or more had alcohol discussed in formulation and 75% an ICD-11 alcohol diagnosis.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.251.topic: Baricitinib dosing in elderly and renal impairment
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.251.setting: Rheumatology, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.251.standard: NICE guidance (2 mg daily if 75 years or older) and BNF (avoid if creatinine clearance <30 ml/min; reduce dose if 30–60 ml/min)

cycle1.result: Of 13 aged 75+ still on baricitinib, 10 on 2 mg and 3 on 4 mg; 4 of 7 started after 75 began on 4 mg; 14 of 16 with creatinine clearance 30–60 ml/min were at some point on 4 mg, 6 still on 4 mg

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.251.other_findings: Suggested adding age and renal function to the prescription format.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.460.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) pre-initiation and ongoing monitoring for lithium, valproate and carbamazepine (16 standards)

cycle1.result: Valproate FBC monitoring within 6 months 92% (other 2018 figures not reported)

cycle2.result: Valproate pre-initiation LFT 35.8%, FBC 41.5%, 6-month monitoring 85.7% and 87.5%; lithium pre-initiation ECG 73.1%, TFT 88.5%, U&E 96.2%, monitoring 100%; carbamazepine pre-initiation 50%, monitoring 100%; all standards improved except valproate FBC monitoring

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.460.other_findings: Only 6 of 16 standards had 100% compliance; pre-initiation monitoring poor for valproate and carbamazepine.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.441.setting: Specialist Support Team (Lancashire and Greater Manchester), Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.441.standard: STOMP prescribing standards: indication and rationale stated, consent, monitoring of response and side effects, review of need for continuation

cycle1.result: Indication and rationale 50%; consent, monitoring and review of continuation each less than 10%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10585.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, Southend Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10585.standard: Documented 4AT for patients aged 65 and over referred to the liaison team

cycle1.result: 5 (7.5%) had a documented 4AT score

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10585.intervention: Educational sessions for MHLT staff and laminated 4AT lanyard prompts
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10585.other_findings: Recommended integrating the 4AT into assessment forms.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.262.setting: Mental Health Inreach Team, HMP Elmley (Category B remand prison)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.262.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists 'Use of licensed medicines for unlicensed applications in psychiatric practice' (2nd edition)

cycle1.result: 82 on off-label quetiapine; 28.1% (23/82) initiated by MHIRT psychiatrists

cycle2.result: 60 on off-label quetiapine; 8.3% (5/60) initiated by MHIRT; licensed drug considered, risks and benefits documented, explained and consent documented 80.0% each; low start dose 100%; baseline physical health 80.0%

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.262.other_findings: Prescriber could not be determined in 17 patients; most off-label prescriptions were started by other prescribers.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.862.setting: High dependency unit and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Sydney
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.862.standard: TGA and Medsafe product information and Therapeutic Guidelines maximum doses: 100% of individual and combined antipsychotic doses within limits

cycle1.result: 13/30 (43.3%) above 100% cumulative maximum; 3 (10%) above maximum for regular antipsychotics; 0/30 for PRN; 18/30 (60%) on 2 antipsychotics, 8/30 (26.6%) on 3, 2/30 (6.6%) on 4

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.862.other_findings: Recommended review of routine PRN antipsychotics and a vital sign monitoring protocol.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10646.standard: National guidelines on ADHD medication initiation, physical health monitoring, follow-up and rating scales

cycle1.result: Pre-medication assessment 100%; regular follow-up 5/7; height and weight plotted 6/7; rating scales returned by parents 0 and schools 3/7

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10646.intervention: Recommendations from previous audit, including a centralised list of service users and retrieval of rating scales

cycle2.result: Pre-medication assessment 100%; regular follow-up 5/7; physical health check within 3 months 100%; height and weight plotted 6/7; rating scales completed by parents and school 6/7; green compliance

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10646.other_findings: Waiting time to start medication increased because of staffing issues.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.137.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after cancer surgery
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.137.setting: Oesophago-gastric unit, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Preston
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.137.standard: NICE: extended pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery

cycle1.result: Pre-2014: 13/92 (14.1%) discharged with 28-day prophylaxis; post-2014: 423/490 (86.3%) (p<0.05); VTE 0.17%

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.137.intervention: Trust-wide policy of 28-day extended VTE prophylaxis after discharge adopted in 2014

cycle2.result: 63/68 (92.6%) received prophylaxis (86.3% to 92.6%, p=0.145); VTE 0%; no bleeding readmissions

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.137.other_findings: No readmissions for bleeding complications in either period.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.301.setting: Memory Assessment Service, East North East Older People's Services, Leeds

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.301.intervention: Formal MAS appointment pathway with defined admin contact points, displayed on posters in admin and memory nurse rooms

cycle2.result: Positive improvement in attendance rate (figures not reported)

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.301.other_findings: Admin team had no pathway to guide appointment management before the project.
